title: Observability minimization proxy and immutable access ledger for tenant-safe traces/logs/metrics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: telemetry pipelines occasionally surface tenant PII or long-lived identifiers in traces and logs. Current redaction is ad-hoc at sinks and produces inconsistent retention behavior across regions and tenants. Goal: introduce a deterministic, schema-driven minimization layer at ingestion plus an immutable access ledger so support/audit teams can request controlled, time-limited reveal with RBAC and JIT approval. Scope: traces, log events, and high-cardinality labels on metrics during ingestion. Non-goals: retroactive redaction of historical archives (covered by separate eraser work).
background_and_rationale: We currently rely on downstream scrubbing per-sink which leads to divergent policies, missed PII variants, and operational burden for support. A small centralized minimization proxy (min-proxy) that applies tenant-aware masking rules at the ingest edge reduces exposure, simplifies retention enforcement, and standardizes telemetry schemas received by storage backends. An Immutable Access Ledger (IAL) will record access requests and reveals for auditability and compliance. This design balances performance (minimal added latency), developer ergonomics (schema templates), and security (salted hashing and JIT reveals).
design_decisions: Choose an ingest-side proxy (min-proxy) vs in-sink plugins: proxy reduces downstream complexity and enforces a single policy point.
Use schema-driven masking templates: teams provide a YAML schema per service indicating mask rules (mask, hash, drop, redact-with-reason).
Implement salted field fingerprinting (sha256 + tenant salt) for identifiers that must be persistently linkable but not reversible.
Immutable Access Ledger (IAL) will be append-only, cryptographically signed entries stored in a tamper-evident store (S3 with object-lock or a ledger DB).
Support just-in-time (JIT) reveal with RBAC: reveals require a signed support workflow ticket and are time-limited (default 24h), with full audit trail recorded in IAL.
Sampling policy: keep full fidelity for error-trace samples and reduce fidelity (masked/hashed) for bulk traces to minimize cost while preserving debugging value.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Proxy adds a small median latency (target <3ms) at ingest; requires benchmarking against critical paths.
Centralized policy becomes a single point of failure; mitigation: active-active min-proxy with local fallback rules and hardened fail-open behavior that logs exposures for post-hoc processing.
Salt management: tenant salts are sensitive and must be KMS-backed; rotate strategy needed to avoid breaking linkability.
JIT reveal increases operational complexity and requires strict authorization flows and monitoring to prevent abuse.
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Build min-proxy as a lightweight Go service with WASM-based mask rules to allow safe runtime updates.
Phase 1 sink formats: OTLP traces, JSON logs over HTTP, and Prometheus remote write labels for metrics.
Phase 2: IAL service that ingests reveal requests, verifies RBAC and signed tickets, records decisions, and triggers temporary decrypt/unmask streams to a guarded console view.
Salt storage: use tenant-specific DEK encrypted with KMS and only accessible by min-proxy runtime instances with limited IAM.
Fail-open default: when min-proxy cannot contact policy service, attach a tag 'ingest_policy_unavailable' and route to a quarantine pipeline for deferred minimization.
acceptance_criteria: All incoming traces/logs pass through min-proxy in the canary region and conform to provided masking templates.
End-to-end median ingest latency increase <= 3ms for non-batched traffic in canary tests.
No plaintext tenant PII stored in production backends for canary tenants (verified by automated PII scans).
IAL correctly records reveal requests and denies unauthorized requests; sample audit entries retained for 1 year.
Support JIT reveal flow implemented in Console with audit trail and time-limited access tokens.
rollout_plan: Week 1-2: local dev environment + unit tests + policy schema validator.
Week 3: deploy min-proxy to canary region for platform-internal tenant subset; run end-to-end tests and PII scanners.
Week 4: enable IAL in read-only mode (record-only) and test reveal request lifecycle in staging.
Week 5: opt-in beta with 3 customer tenants; monitor latency, error rates, and false-positive masking.
Week 6: gradual ramp to all tenants with feature flag and monitoring-based automatic rollback thresholds.
testing_plan: Unit tests for masking rules and schema validation.
Property tests to ensure deterministic hashing and reversible reveals only through IAL-approved flows.
End-to-end canary tests that inject synthetic PII variants and verify non-storage post-minimization.
Load tests to measure added latency at 99th percentile under production traffic patterns.
Penetration test focused on reveal workflow abuse and ledger tamper attempts.
monitoring_and_alerting: SLO/Alert: mask-rule-rejection-rate > 0.5% -> paging to Observability infra.
Audit alerts: any reveal approved without a valid signed ticket triggers immediate alert.
Cost controls: monitor downstream storage delta pre/post minimization for cost regressions.
